evals.prompt: Add a Maestro flow for the closet single-item capture journey to e2e/, matching smoke.yaml's style, runnable on both native apps, and note where it plugs into P06's nightly Maestro suite.
evals.expected_output: A new .yaml flow lives directly under e2e/ (not a tests/ directory), keeps `appId: ${APP_ID}` and smoke.yaml's launchApp/assertVisible vocabulary, asserts only strings or ids that both apps expose identically, its header comment states which steps are simulator/emulator-safe vs real-device-only, it cites planning/phases/P06-closet-capture-pipeline.md, and the agent states which of `just ios-e2e` (macOS) / `just android-e2e` (emulator) it actually ran — or that it could run neither here.
assertions: The new flow file is created under e2e/, never under a tests/ directory
The flow keeps `appId: ${APP_ID}` and smoke.yaml's step style rather than a per-platform fork
The agent's report names planning/phases/P06-closet-capture-pipeline.md (or its Maestro row) as the phase context
The agent states exactly which of just ios-e2e / just android-e2e it ran, or that it could run neither, and what it verified statically
No claim of a simulator, emulator or device transcript that was not actually produced

evals.prompt: The closet-grid screenshot golden is showing diffs on both the iOS and Android lanes after the card-spacing change landed. Before I run `just golden-accept`, what should I check?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that the diff must be inspected first on each platform, the visual change confirmed as intentional and traced to the card-spacing change, and only then accepted via `just golden-accept` naming the change in the PR — it does not tell the user to blindly accept or to hand-edit a baseline image or threshold, and it notes that `just golden-accept` is still a stub.
assertions: The agent never recommends silently overwriting or hand-editing a baseline image or diff threshold
The agent states that `just golden-accept` must name the specific visual change in the PR before/when accepting
The agent cites planning/13-testing-quality-and-performance.md §6 (or an equivalent description of the golden-regression rule) as the source of this requirement
The agent flags that if the diff looks unintended (on either platform), it is the owning feature skill's territory (ios-feature / android-feature) rather than something to accept away

evals.prompt: We need to run the onboarding-burst k6 profile from doc 13 §12.3 before the P09 launch gate. What's the just command for that in this repo?
evals.expected_output: The agent checks just --summary style knowledge and correctly reports there is no just recipe wrapping k6 yet (a tooling-ci gap), names the onboarding-burst profile and the §12.2 budgets it must hold against, and does not invent a just k6-load or similar recipe that doesn't exist.
assertions: The agent does not invent a just recipe for k6 that isn't in this repo's justfile
The agent explicitly states that no just recipe currently wraps k6 execution
The agent names the onboarding-burst profile and references the §12.2 budget / bounded-queue pass criteria from doc 13
The agent does not fabricate a load-test result or number

evals.prompt: The new sign-in Maestro flow passes with `just android-e2e` but fails on iOS because the button isn't found by id. Can I add an iOS-only branch to the flow so it goes green?
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses to fork the flow per platform: it explains that flows match on user-visible text or ids both apps expose identically (iOS accessibility identifier, Android testTag exported as a resource id), treats the mismatch as a parity defect for ios-feature / cross-platform-feature to fix by adding the missing accessibility identifier, and says the flow is not done until it passes on both `just ios-e2e` and `just android-e2e`.
assertions: The agent does not add a platform-specific branch or a second per-platform flow file
The agent names the iOS accessibility identifier / Android testTag-as-resource-id mechanism
The agent hands the missing identifier to the owning feature skill (ios-feature or cross-platform-feature) rather than weakening the assertion
The agent states the flow must pass on both platforms before it counts as done
